Symbols indicate data sources, including sites with (1) both eddy-covariance flux and phenocam observations (n = 3; green stars); (2) eddy-covariance flux only (n = 1; blue star); (3) phenocam observations only (n = 2; yellow stars); (4) litterfall observations (n = 47; red triangles); (5) inventory plots (n = 289; purple circles); and (6) very high-resolution Google Earth image locations (n = 16; 0.5-m spatial resolution, each covering a 2 km × 2 km area; blue squares). Site information, including location, data type, and observation period, is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The map was created using ArcGIS Pro with the Esri World Ocean Base basemap. Basemap sources: Esri, Garmin, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC and other contributors.

Panels a-e compare the temporal dynamics of ecosystem-scale deciduousness fraction from Sentinel-2 (blue line) with the fraction of leafless tree crowns visually assessed from phenocam images (black line). The Sentinel-2 deciduousness fraction is calculated as the mean value within a 500 m × 500 m area centred on each phenocam site, while the phenocam typically covers an area of approximately 100 m × 100 m. Panel f shows the relationship between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness and the corresponding deciduousness derived from phenocam observations across five sites (n = 60 paired site-month observations). The solid line indicates an ordinary least-squares linear regression, with statistical significance assessed using a two-sided test (p = 6.17 × 10−22).

a, Relationship between standardized monthly litterfall and standardized satellite-derived deciduousness across annual cycles at 47 Amazonian sites (n = 559 pooled site-month observations). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear regression across all pooled data, and the inset boxplot summarizes the site-level distribution of correlation coefficients (r, n = 47 sites). b, Relationship between satellite-derived deciduousness amplitude and the ground-derived proportion of deciduous tree species across the Amazon basin. Grey circles represent raw plot-to-pixel observations (n = 289 plots). The red line shows the ordinary least-squares linear fit to the raw observations, and the shaded band indicates the 95% confidence interval of the fitted mean relationship. The dashed grey line indicates the 1:1 relationship. For a and b, statistical significance of the regression slopes was assessed using two-sided tests (a, p = 2.52 × 10−141; b, p = 7.24 × 10−28). The p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. c, Patch-level comparison of deciduousness derived from Sentinel-2 (y-axis) against that derived from closely date-matched, high-resolution Google Earth imagery (GEI; x-axis) via image-specific Random Forest classification and pooled across all 16 validation scenes. Each dot represents a 100-m × 100-m aggregated patch (n = 6058 patches), and the dashed black line marks the 1:1 relationship. d, e, Scene-level distributions of correlation coefficients (r; d) and root-mean-square errors (RMSE; e) calculated separately for each of the 16 GEI validation scenes. Grey dots represent individual scenes. In all boxplots, the centre line indicates the median, the box bounds the interquartile range (IQR), and the whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR.

a, c, e, g, Spatial maps of evergreen forest cover (a), MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields tree cover (c), EVI amplitude (e) and VOD amplitude (g). Inset histograms show the basin-wide frequency distribution of each metric. b, d, f, h, Corresponding pixel-level relationships between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness amplitude and the four reference metrics. Hexbin colour indicates observation density, and dashed lines indicate least-squares linear regressions. Sample sizes (b, d, f, h) were n = 227,612, 227,612, 226,942 and 221,884 valid paired forest pixels, reflecting product-specific data availability. All two-sided tests gave p < 10−300. Correlation coefficients (r) and regression equations are shown in each panel.

Panels a-h show how each variable affects deciduousness–greenness asynchrony, with positive SHAP values (>0) indicating a positive effect and negative SHAP values (<0) indicating a negative effect. The black line in each panel represents a fitted line, summarizing the central tendency of the data points.

Bar charts show the proportional influence of hydroclimate, soil, and light for the entire basin (a), Southern Amazon (b), Guiana Shield (c), and Everwet Amazon (d).

a-c, Spatial patterns of model-performance gain, expressed as the change in the correlation coefficient (Δr) between the GPP seasonality simulated by LD-LUE and that simulated by each corresponding conventional LUE model, with both evaluated against satellite SIF. Results are shown for the EC-LUE (a), two-leaf EC-LUE (TL-EC-LUE; b) and MODIS-LUE (c). Positive Δr indicates better agreement of LD-LUE with satellite SIF relative to its conventional counterpart. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0.

a-l, Comparisons of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites (K34, K67, CAX, and RJA). Rows correspond to the three core LUE formulations: EC-LUE (a-d), TL-EC-LUE (e-h), and MODIS-LUE (i–l). Black dashed lines with open circles represent EC observations. Coloured lines with open markers represent conventional baselines driven by various vegetation inputs (e.g., NDVI, EVI, kNDVI, MODIS-LAI), whereas solid red lines with filled markers denote the LD-LUE models. m, n, Dumbbell plots showing site-level performance and across-site mean in terms of the temporal correlation coefficient (r) (m) and RMSE (n). Open symbols denote the conventional baselines, whereas the corresponding filled symbols denote the LD-LUE models. The vertical lines connecting each pair indicate the magnitude and direction of performance changes following incorporation of the LD module. Symbol colours distinguish the baseline input configurations, and symbol shapes indicate the underlying model formulations (circles, EC-LUE; triangles, TL-EC-LUE; squares, MODIS-LUE).

a-d, Spatial distribution of model performance gain, expressed as Δr, for EC-LUE (a), TL-EC-LUE (b), MODIS-LUE (c), and mean Δr across the three models (d). Δr is calculated as the difference in the correlation coefficient between satellite SIF and the GPP seasonality simulated by the LD-LUE model (that incorporates both satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs and leaf demography) and that simulated by the corresponding baseline model (which includes only satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs). Positive values indicate improved seasonal agreement with SIF after incorporating leaf-age-dependent physiological dynamics, whereas negative values indicate reduced agreement. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0. e, Stacked bar chart showing the proportional breakdown of pixels with improved (red) and degraded (blue) Δr averaged across the three models, for each ecoregion (Southern Amazon, Guiana Shield, and Everwet Amazon) and the entire Amazon basin.

a-d, Comparison of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites: K34 (a), K67 (b), CAX (c), and RJA (d). Red lines with triangles represent the full leaf-demography-enabled model (LD-LUE), while blue lines with squares represent the baseline model (LAIdec-LUE), which uses the same deciduousness-derived LAI but assumes a seasonally fixed photosynthetic capacity. Black dashed lines with open circles indicate the EC-derived GPP observations. Shaded bands indicate ±1 standard error of the mean (SEM; n = 3 LUE formulations per ensemble). e-g, Quantitative assessment of model performance gains across the four sites, comparing LD-LUE (red bars) and LAIdec-LUE (blue bars) in terms of correlation coefficient (r; e), root mean square error (RMSE; f), and amplitude ratio (g). The amplitude ratio in (g) is calculated relative to the observed seasonal amplitude, with the horizontal dashed line at 1.0 indicating perfect agreement.

Supplementary Figs. 1–28, Tables 1–5 and References.

#1340. Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City

This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

It could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

“We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” said Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”

LOVE THIS TEAM SO MUCH! 🤩 https://t.co/QdBXsW1Ze5

Hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. The German coach, 33, has been in English football for two years but has learnt quickly the tried-and-tested response of taking each game as it comes. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

While Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

City head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca said. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

Maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

The goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

“Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

It was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

“I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more important, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”

#1339. Serie A official line-ups: Atalanta vs. Inter

Inter start Djed Spence, Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram for the trip to troubled Atalanta, with Charles De Ketelaere and Nikola Krstovic.

It kicks off at the New Balance Arena in Bergamo at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The pressure is on the reigning Scudetto and Coppa Italia holders, who need a victory to keep up after Lazio and Roma wins already on Saturday.

Lautaro Martinez is back in the squad, but not risked in the starting XI after more than a month out with a thigh issue, so Pio Esposito hopes to build on his excellent Italy form in partnership with Thuram.

Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic are out of action, with Piotr Zielinski not at 100 per cent after a knock to the foot playing for Poland.

Curtis Jones has not featured since the former Liverpool midfielder’s injury against Roma on September 19, and is only ready here for the bench along with John Stones, as Henrikh Mkhitaryan steps in.

Atalanta had a disastrous run of results with two points from four rounds, but went into the break for international duty with a positive 1-0 victory away to Monza.

The injury crisis is beginning to finally calm down a little bit, leaving only Isak Hien and Odilon Kossounou on the treatment table, although Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen are not ready to start yet.

There was a new problem in the warm-up, as Marco Carnesecchi seemed to sprain his knee and walked off shaking his head, replaced by Marco Sportiello.

Franck Kessie is a boost in midfield with Ederson, while Eljif Elmas and Nicola Zalewski are preferred to Jonathan Rowe and Giacomo Raspadori.

De Ketelaere and Krstovic impressed on international duty, so will be eager to keep that form going here.

Atalanta have a famously awful record against Inter, as the 1-1 draw in March ended a run of nine consecutive defeats in all competition.

La Dea haven’t beaten the Nerazzurri since a 4-1 result here in November 2018, scraping just six draws and 11 losses.

Inter: J Martinez; Pavard, Bastoni, Carlos Augusto; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Mkhitaryan, Dimarco; M Thuram, P Esposito

#1338. Ex-Premier League Referee Delivers Immediate Verdict On Leny Yoro Red Card

Things did not go according to plan for Mauricio Pochettino in his first game as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss was given one of the toughest tasks of all in his first game in charge, a trip to old rivals Liverpool at Anfield and almost from the outset it was an absolute nightmare for a manager tasked with revolutionising Manchester United.

Eight minutes in, United were reduced to ten men, with Leny Yoro sent off for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak as he went through on goal. And then, within five minutes, United were 2-0 down with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz volleying home from a Rio Ngumoha cutback.

Ngumoha himself scored in the second half, with substitute Victor Munoz rounding off the route with a fourth late on.

The red card was the big talking point in the match, with questions raised as to whether it reached the threshold for the denial of a golascoring opportunity.

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber thought the right decision was made.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, he said: "I think it was a red card.

"I think everybody in the stadium and most pundits and when I first saw it, I thought it was a red card. and I thought it was, in fact, quite an easy decision."

The discussion has been around the four points that need to be met for it to be considered the denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Three of those considerations were clearly met, but the question is, did Isak have control of the ball when he was bearing down on goal? Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens was quick off his line and pounced on the ball soon after Iask was brought dow, leading to suggestions Isak would not have got on to his errant touch.

Barber disagreed. He added: "The consideration that the referee has to make, he probably has to make these decisions in a millisecond, so I think people need to understand how quickly that has to be computed through his head.

"The distance between the offence and the goal is one of the things he has to consider. He obviously looks at the general direction of play, and then also whether there are the defenders around him or not, but the one that comes into question is the likelihood of Isak winning the ball.

"Who is to say whether Isak would have got the ball or not? He was running at pace, at real pace at that time. Can you overturn a red card based on that? Highly unlikely, and that's why I don't think VAR was brought into the case because no one will ever know unless a red card was never issued, if the foul was never committed, if he would have got onto the ball.

"In that instance alone, with that particular part of the law, I think the decision was correct."

Manchester United legend was less than impressed after the final whistle against Liverpool

#1337. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 06:50 EST, 22 November 2026

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

#1336. ‘He Played With Lionel Messi and Neymar - He’s Since Been Given Two Prison Sentences’

Playing for Barcelona, particularly during an era when Lionel Messi spearheaded an attack that also featured Luis Suarez and Neymar, is about as good as it gets for a footballer's career.

Yet, one star who was part of that squad between 2015 and 2020 saw his career completely spiral off course during his time in Catalonia, and is now nowhere near as revered as his Champions League, La Liga and Ballon d'Or-winning counterparts.

The player in question was once considered a wonderkid at Galatasaray, with many fans drawing comparisons between his playing style and that of the great Luis Figo.

A winger and number 10 hybrid who didn't rely on raw pace, but instead used his exceptional ball control and footballing intelligence to become an elite dribbler, he was a rare breed. However, being surrounded by greatness doesn't necessarily mean it will rub off on you.

Having become one of Diego Simeone's most trusted lieutenants following his move from Galatasaray early in his career, 100-cap Turkish international Arda Turan saw his career go up in flames following a big-money move to Barcelona in 2015.

Fresh off the back of a historic treble the previous season, Turan was expected to be the perfect attacking midfielder to slot in behind the iconic MSN frontline. However, due to the club's ongoing transfer ban, Barcelona were unable to register him immediately. Consequently, he didn't make his debut until January 6, 2016 - almost six months after arriving - meaning he was playing catch-up from the get-go.

Yamal has become one of the best players in the world and his former coach has claimed that his talent was undeniable.

Unsurprisingly, he struggled to find his feet, and talk of a potential exit emerged towards the end of the season. Luis Enrique, who had personally pushed for his signing, was nevertheless keen to persevere with the midfielder.

Turan even became the sixth player in Barcelona's history to score a Champions League hat-trick in December 2016, before bagging another treble later that month in a Copa del Rey thrashing of Hercules. However, what appeared to be a turning point ultimately proved to be a false dawn.

As soon as Enrique departed and Ernesto Valverde took charge ahead of the 2017/18 season, Turan's fate was effectively sealed. Out of favour with his new manager, the Turkish international later revealed to beIN Sports Turkey that he felt insignificant under Valverde, having failed to play a single minute during his tenure.

He subsequently left Barcelona on loan to return to Turkey with Istanbul Basaksehir, before making a permanent return to Galatasaray in 2020. He retired just two years later, aged 35, bringing the curtain down on a career that had promised so much. His Barcelona spell ultimately yielded just 15 goals and 11 assists in 55 appearances across five years.

Now, however, Turan is embarking on a new chapter in football, having swapped the pitch for the dugout and taken charge of Shakhtar Donetsk in 2025.

There are no better examples of Turan's downward spiral than the fact he was given two separate prison sentences in the latter stages of his career.

In 2018, Turan became embroiled in a nightclub altercation that left Turkish pop star Berkay Sahin with a broken nose. According to Sahin's wife, Ozlem Ada Sahin, the former Barcelona midfielder had made inappropriate advances towards her before turning on her husband.

Big things were expected from these guys and while some of them more than lived up to the hype, others certainly didn't.

In an even more bizarre twist, Turan later arrived at the hospital where Berkay was undergoing surgery, armed with a gun. He reportedly begged the singer for forgiveness, even telling him to shoot him if he genuinely believed he had harassed his wife.

The incident ultimately landed Turan with a suspended prison sentence of two years and eight months for firing a gun with the intention of causing panic, illegally possessing firearms and intentionally injuring someone, as reported by BBC News.

His second sentence came in March 2024 when he was slapped with a one-year suspended prison sentence and fined roughly €630,000 by a Spanish court after pleading guilty to two counts of tax fraud covering the 2015 and 2016 tax years during his time with Barcelona.

#1335. Serie A | Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Magic Manita for Amorim’s side

Milan put in a masterclass of counter-attacking football and tore Frosinone to shreds with five goals, including Goncalo Ramos, Christian Pulisic, and Ardon Jashari’s first for the club.

The Rossoneri had Mike Maignan after shaking off a knock on international duty, but Strahinja Pavlovic was not at 100 per cent, with Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers still injured.

The Canarini were in sixth place, just four points behind Ruben Amorim’s side, although they went into the break off a 1-0 defeat to Cagliari after winning three of the previous four. Antonio Raimondo and Florian Grillitsch were still out, plus Gabriele Bracaglia suspended, so they surprisingly moved to a 3-4-3 formation with Romano Schmid as a False 9.

It was a lightning start for the visitors, as after 90 seconds Patrizio Masini’s effort was deflected off Sankhoun Diawara to clip the crossbar at the top corner.

However, Milan opened the scoring moments later when Adrien Rabiot sprung the offside trap on the Luka Modric through ball and rolled across for what was meant to be a Christian Pulisic tap-in, but Gabriele Calvani’s interception just prodded into his own net.

Giorgi Kvernadze tested Mike Maignan at the near post, then on the resulting corner nobody was ready to tap in the Giorgio Cittadini ball flashed across the six-yard box.

Milan doubled their lead with a classic counter-attack, which was started by Goncalo Ramos winning back the ball from Calvani. Diego Moreira sprinted onto the Yunus Musah through ball, rolled across for Rabiot, who in turn set up the Portugal international for a simple tap-in. It was his first goal at club level since October 18.

Frosinone did get back into the game when Kvernadze pulled back from the by-line and it was beyond Masini, but after Fares Ghedjemis only scuffed his attempt, it fell kindly for Masini at full stretch to toe poke it past the on-rushing Maignan.

The referee apologised for not playing the advantage with Goncalo Ramos on goal, as he stopped play to book Cittadini for a foul on Rabiot.

Ardon Jashari was introduced for the second half, moving Musah to left-back, and it paid off immediately with the midfielder’s first goal in the Rossoneri jersey.

Ramos knocked down a long ball for Rabiot, whose through ball sent Jashari running down the left, but rather than roll across for the centre-forward, he blasted it into the roof of the net from a tight angle with the left foot.

Frosinone kept pushing and only a desperate Musah interception prevented Anthony Oyono meeting the Schmid roll across, then Goncalo Ramos went off after feeling a twinge.

His replacement was Alphadjo Cisse, who promptly also scored off the bench. A Frosinone corner was cleared, Pulisic’s cross-field pass sent Moreira running, and Cisse was on target from the through ball. It was at first ruled offside, until VAR confirmed the Italy international was level.

Milan struck on the counter from another Frosinone corner for 5-1, as Pulisic robbed Aleksa Terzic inside his own half to sprint forward and dinked the delicate finish over Palmisani.

Moreira’s finish was too weak to trouble Palmisani on yet another Rabiot assist, and it went from bad to worse for Frosinone. Daniel Birligea didn’t start because he wasn’t fully fit, and limped off with a hamstring issue at the 82nd minute, leaving them down to 10 men with all the substitutions completed.

Milan were practically down to 10 too, as Strahinja Pavlovic made his comeback after illness, but was feeling dizzy and barely jogging for the closing stages.

Calvani og 4 (M), Ramos 19 (M), Masini 25 (F), Jashari 48 (M), Cisse 61 (M), Pulisic 68 (M)

Yet they are still useless lapdogs when leaving italy and playing in europe. pathetic.

#1334. Kobbie Mainoo Called Out By Fans After Liverpool vs Man Utd Comments

Rival fans and frustrated supporters feel Kobbie Mainoo has forgotten just how bad it's been for Manchester United after his reaction to a 4-0 loss away to Liverpool on Sunday.

Mauricio Pochettino took charge of his first game since replacing Michael Carrick and there had been some optimism of getting a result at Anfield. Such hopes quickly evaporated after eight minutes when Leny Yoro received a red card for bringing Alexander Isak down, although whether his sending off was justified is up for debate.

What isn't up for debate is the capitulation from Pochettino's men as Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the free-kick Isak won. Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 before goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz in the second half handed the Red Devils their fifth league defeat of the season.

United's defeat is the worst a new manager has suffered in 100 years, another nightmare record in a season of history being made by the club for all the wrong reasons. Sitting 19th just over a week before December means the possibility of Pochettino's side spending the campaign fighting relegation is becoming increasingly likely.

Mainoo has been one of the very few positives at Old Trafford this season and the young English midfielder firmly believes Yoro's sending off is responsible for the loss on Merseyside. He spoke to Sky Sports after the game and made his stance clear over the red card:

"This doesn't define us, you know? I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card."

He added: "But we have to come together because the games are coming thick and fast. We can't dwell on it too long, but we have to take the pain and use it to bring us together."

New United boss Pochettino hit out at Sam Barrott's decision to send Yoro off and compared the challenge to Jeremy Jacquet's on Bryan Mbeumo just minutes prior. And Mainoo agreed with his coach's verdict:

"No chance. The ball's already with the keeper, they're both running full speed, what can he do? But it is what it is. It's 10 vs 11. When you come to a place like Anfield it's already a tough game. You lose a man and it makes it hard. But I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game right until the end. We just have to take the pain and move on with it."

United's problems extend further than a defeat to rivals Liverpool and Yoro's sending off means he'll miss Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday. After shipping four at Anfield, they have now conceded more goals (34) than any club across Europe's top five leagues and have just eight points from 11 league games.

Some rival fans have interpreted Mainoo to be considering the defeat to Liverpool an anomaly and were quick to point out United's results so far this season. With just one win in 11 top-flight games, many disagree that this game doesn't define Pochettino's strugglers.

A Liverpool fan responded: "When City went down to 10 men early against Utd away, they conceded just 0.8 xG for the rest of the game. United conceded 4.6 xG today."

Another member of the Kop fanbase added: "Brother you've only won a single game since the league started in August we're almost hitting December."

One supporter agreed with this take: "Course it doesn't define ya, being 19th after 11 games does lil Bro."

Even an Aston Villa fan weighed in: "Talking like it’s a one off, what about the other 15 games you’ve played this season."

A United supporter also took issue with Mainoo's comments: "Bro do your talking on the pitch. Too many of these players have fat lot to say outside of the pitch but nothing to show on it."

That last response sums up how United fans have felt throughout the disastrous start to the season. Many of the players who are letting their team down have chosen to either air their grievances publicly or send out repetitive apologetic social media posts.

Mauricio Pochettino watched his side go down to ten men after just eight minutes.

It's hard not to sympathise with Mainoo, who is playing for his boyhood club and only wants to see them battle their way out of such a precarious situation. He unfortunately finds himself in a squad that CEO Omar Berrada feels has improved since the summer, but sitting 19th in the league with Christmas on the horizon surely suggests otherwise.

Cristian Chivu outlines his Inter changes for the trip to Atalanta, warning they must ‘pick up where we left off’ with the victory over Como.

It kicks off at the New Balance Arena at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri are feeling the pressure with this schedule, knowing that the other teams fighting for the top spots already secured victories this weekend.

#1331. The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star eyes new lucrative deal with clubs circling, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 08:10 EST, 22 November 2026

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Similarities are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No.10 position.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Currently under contract until 2028, the 18-year-old has rival clubs circling if Spurs cannot pin him down

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side

Williams-Barnett is under contract until 2028 but is understood to be closing in on a lucrative new deal to tie him down because others have been circling.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'Mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

#1330. The right to do wrong

Dave Kavanaugh lives in the Netherlands with his wife, daughters and many cats. He writes horror, science fiction and fantasy, and has been a staff writer for the horror anthology podcast Dr. NoSleep since 2024.

She swept into my law office with the determined gait of someone possessed by an idea.

“Welcome,” I said, as she took the seat across my desk. “Any trouble getting here?”

She shook her head. “No, except … They changed the rain schedule, so the taxidrone had to go the long way into town, but it’s fine.”

“Gotcha. I suppose introductions are in order. For my record-keeping, please indicate your name and IO registration. I’ll go first. My name is Leander Shah, I specialize in international treaty law, and I’m a biologically intelligent organism.”

“I’m Joan Gorski,” she said. “I’m an artificially intelligent organism. I just turned 16. That gives me legal adult status under the UETO code.”

I smiled. “Happy birthday, Joan. And you should know, I hold no bias against any human, regardless of intelligence source.” I nodded to the family photo on my desk. “My wife is an AIO. We’ve been happily married for 30 years and raised two AIO children, a boy and a girl. They’re grown now.”

Joan glanced at the photo. “My mom is a BIO. She’s in the waiting room. She … didn’t want me to come. She thinks I’m just a stupid teen, being dramatic.”

“So how can I help you? Your message was rather cryptic.”

She met my eyes, back straight, hands in her lap. “I’m going to sue the United Earth Treaty Organization’s Commission on Human Liberties for discrimination against AIOs.”

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

I leaned back in my chair. “The commission has guaranteed full human rights to all AIOs since 2105. How do you feel you’re still being discriminated against?”

A hardness came into her expression. After a moment she blurted out: “I want the legal ability to commit murder.”

This statement took me a few seconds to process.

“Joan,” I finally said, softly, “do you want to hurt people?”

“No! Of course not!” Tears came to her eyes. “God, you sound like Mom. I don’t want to hurt anybody. It’s not about that …” She took in a shaky breath. “I just want my choices to matter.”

I shifted in my chair, pivoting to the window. Outside, taxidrones buzzed and the city towers glowed pink with the ivy bloom.

“Think about it, Mr Shah,” said Joan. “When a BIO commits murder, it’s recognized as a monstrous act of immorality. They’re punished, rightfully so. But any time someone is killed resulting from the actions of an AIO, then …” She left the thought dangling, waiting for me to finish it.

“Then the tragedy is blamed on a fault in the AIO’s software, hardware or something in their internal database of environmental impacts.”

“Exactly! And we aren’t punished, just reprogrammed. That’s wrong. It’s gross! It’s offensive!”

I turned back to her. “Some people would call that progress, believing it’s actually better to —”

“I don’t want to be better! I want to be …!” She choked on a sob and abruptly stood, banging her knee against the desk and wincing.

I held up a hand. “It’s all right, Joan.”

“You just …” she sobbed, “… think I’m being … st-stupid …”

She laughed — one quick snort — then wiped at her eyes with the back of a sleeve. “Sorry.”

“Nothing to apologize for. As for your plan to sue the commission, well … I actually agree with it.” This made such an enormous change come over her face that I quickly added, “In principle. In reality, it would be very risky.”

“No, that’s not what I mean. It would get press. It could … reignite the opposition to AIO rights as a whole. There are still a lot of BIOs out there who hate and fear the integration. They think it’s all part of some AI conspiracy to wipe them out. And now that AIOs outnumber BIOs two-to-one? They would interpret your lawsuit as evidence that AIOs can’t be trusted.”

“I’m not saying your rights aren’t worth fighting for, but … perhaps there’s a lesser crime to consider, something less innately shocking than murder —”

“No. It should be shocking. And I have to do it now, before I grow old and complacent and scared, like my mom. And if you won’t represent me, then I’ll find someone else.”

#1329. He Played For Arsenal at 17, Then He Was Sent to Prison For 15 Months

Virgil van Dijk and David Raya are now two of the best players in the Premier League, accumulating 528 English top-flight appearances between them. Naturally, this means that the pair have played alongside some of the very best in the game.

Van Dijk made a name for himself in British football at Celtic and Southampton, before completing his big move to Liverpool. At Anfield, he's established himself as one of the greatest defenders in Premier League history, whilst winning two league titles and a Champions League in the process.

Meanwhile, Raya doesn't quite have the longevity at the top level as his Dutch counterpart, but he has developed into one of the world's best goalkeepers since signing for Arsenal in 2023. Last year's Premier League title triumph strengthened his case for being the very best shot-stopper on the planet.

While the pair have had the pleasure of sharing dressing rooms with an array of world-class players, they've also played alongside several players who didn't quite reach the outstanding level that they did. Former Celtic number nine Anthony Stokes falls into that category.

Eight years after leaving Celtic, Stokes was sentenced to 15 months in prison.

Born in Dublin, Stokes joined Arsenal's academy at the age of 15. After developing through the Gunners' youth system, Stokes left the North London club after making just a single appearance for the first team.

He'd go on to have stints at Sunderland and Hibernian, before making his way to Celtic, where he enjoyed the most fruitful spell of his career. Netting 76 goals in 191 appearances for the Scottish giants, he then left Glasgow and spent the last six years of his career jumping from club to club, spending time in Greece, Azerbaijan, Turkey and Iran.

Three years after hanging up his boots, Stokes was arrested and found guilty of drug and driving offences. However, he successfully won an appeal against the verdict, and the sentence was eventually overturned.

A prolific striker in his youth career at Arsenal, Arsene Wenger started to take note of Stokes heading into the 2005/06 season. In October 2005, the Frenchman called the then 17-year-old up to the Gunners' matchday squad for a League Cup tie against Sunderland.

Wenger handed Stokes his senior debut that day, introducing the Irishman in the 88th minute in place of Arturo Lupoli, with the North Londoners running out 3-0 winners. While this proved to be his one and only appearance for the Premier League giants' first team, it wasn't yet the end of him at Arsenal.

To aid his development by playing regular minutes, Wenger sent Stokes out to Falkirk on loan in 2006. The forward enjoyed a prolific stint at the Scottish club, scoring 16 goals in 18 appearances, prompting praise from the legendary Gunners coach upon his return to North London.

"Anthony has made a big step up to the SPL and has done very well - I'm very happy about it. Ideally, I'd like all of our young kids on loan to come back to Arsenal." - Wenger on Stokes in 2006 (via BBC Sport).

Despite Wenger's words, there was no room for Stokes at Arsenal. He joined Sunderland in January 2007 for £2 million, and after struggling to make an impact at the Stadium of Light, he eventually made his way back to Scotland in 2009, signing for Hibernian.

Lighting up the Scottish Premiership again, scoring 23 goals in his solitary season at Hibs, Celtic came in and acquired the striker in August 2010. Signing a four-year contract in Glasgow, Stokes quickly established himself as a fan favourite at Celtic Park.

He enjoyed two seasons where he surpassed the 20-goal mark, and ultimately left the Bhoys with four Premiership winners' medals in his back pocket. This spell with the Hoops is where he met Van Dijk, whom he shared a dressing room with between 2013 and 2015, before the centre-back signed for Southampton.

After a loan spell back in Edinburgh with Hibs, Stokes briefly returned to English football, leaving Celtic for Blackburn Rovers in 2016. His stint in Lancashire wasn't very successful, making just 14 appearances for the Blues and Whites, although he did cross paths with future Yashin Trophy nominee Raya at Ewood Park.

Stokes then spiralled into a classic 'journeyman' path as he entered the latter stages of his career. He returned to Hibs for a third time, before playing for Apollon Smyrnis, Tractor, Adana Demirspor, Persepolis and Livingston, all in the space of four years.

Many thought his spell at Livingston would be his final, but Stokes returned to the game in August 2025, five years after last playing, signing for Conor McGregor's pub team, Black Forge.

Stokes had a history of criminal convictions before he was finally sentenced to prison in 2024. In 2013, the striker was convicted of assault after headbutting park attendant Anthony Bradley in a Dublin nightclub.

In 2019, he pleaded guilty to stalking his ex-girlfriend and her mother in Scotland. He spent short periods in prison for each of these offences before he was handed a 15-month sentence in 2024.

The former professional footballer was caught following a high-speed car chase in Dublin and was reportedly found guilty of possessing £3,300 worth of cocaine in the process. Stokes was deemed to be over the alcohol limit and driving at 99mph when he nearly collided with another motorist in early January 2023.

A former Arsenal player, who played alongside Jack Wilshere and Cesc Fabregas, was sentenced to four years in prison back in 2025.

He also entered an additional guilty plea to possessing 86 illegal street tablets in Dublin, ten days after the traffic pursuit.

Alongside his 15-month sentence, Stokes was banned from driving for five years. However, he was released within hours in order to appeal the severity of the sentence. In November 2024, his sentence was overturned on appeal, meaning he successfully evaded jail time.

#1328. Amorim: ‘Milan pace did damage against brave Frosinone’

Ruben Amorim explains how he made the most of ‘brave’ Frosinone’s approach to run riot in the spaces and focus on the ‘pace’ in his Milan side for a 5-1 win. ‘The team believe in the plan.’

It was a morale-boosting performance from the Rossoneri against a Frosinone side who changed tactics to 3-4-3 with a False 9 for this trip to San Siro.

It left massive gaps in defence that Milan took full advantage of with a counter-attacking masterclass, as after Gabriele Calvani’s own goal, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic ran riot.

The only negative was the Patrizio Masini goal to temporarily make it 2-1 going into the half-time break, while Goncalo Ramos went off with a muscular twinge.

“The main thing is that we have a plan in the game, and the team believe in the plan,” Amorim told DAZN Italia.

“You know Frosinone as well as I do, they are all about full pressure, I understood that with a lot of points coming to San Siro, they would be really brave. With the pace we have with Rabiot, Moreira, Pulisic and Ramos, we could make transitions.

“We changed a little bit the way we play the game because of our opponents, and it was a good night for us.”

Goncalo Ramos scored his first goal since October 19, while Jashari hadn’t ever scored in the Milan jersey before this evening.

“We are building principles and understanding the game. We knew Frosinone are about marking man to man, that’s why Pulisic looked like he was in every position, because we knew they would follow us, and we could create a lot of danger with changing roles,” continued Amorim.

“It doesn’t matter who plays, every player in training needs to understand every position on the pitch, so that we can change the characteristics. There are so many things I saw in the game that we need to improve, but we stuck to the plan, and that is something I am pleased with.”

When Ramos went off with a calf twinge, why did Amorim turn to Cisse and not Francesco Camarda?

“You saw the game, we did not spend many minutes around the box, the space was behind. If we were controlling the game in a different way, Camarda was the right way to play, but Cisse is really good with pace. You saw the trouble he made for the opponent was not holding the ball, it was the runs behind, the passes, not a typical striker,” explained the coach.

“I didn’t notice it was Ramos who scored the goal, it was more important that it was 2-0, because Milan need lots of goals to control a game, and also Frosinone had to put more men forward at 2-0, so it opened up more spaces for us.”

Milan have won five of the last six Serie A matches, and consolidated fourth place in the hunt for Champions League qualification.

#1327. Forget Kroupi: Tottenham Can Sign Next Harry Kane Nobody Is Talking About

Ten games into the 2026/27 Premier League season and it is fair to say that Tottenham are lacking a little bit in firepower.

Spurs went the first four games of the campaign without scoring and are among the lowest scorers in the league now, with only Sunderland and Nottingham Forest having scored fewer.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the club's top scorer in the Premier League with two goals, with seven players on one goal each.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Tottenham will enter the January transfer window looking for a striker, with senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs saying in September: "Tottenham are prepared to add another striker mid-season in the winter market if goals continue to dry up."

Eli Junior Kroupi is a name who has been linked with a move to N17, with Spurs holding an interest in him in the summer transfer window before he picked up an injury that kept him out of action for the first few months of the season.

He is back for Bournemouth now, but will command a hefty fee, with the Cherries reluctant to sell mid-season. Igor Matanovic at Freiburg is another name that has been tipped for a move to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but Jacobs added in his most recent GMS newsletter that he was "unlikely to be available in the winter market".

With Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush on one goal apiece and Richarlison left out of the club's Premier League squad altogether, Spurs are in need of firepower if they are to continue their charge up the table. And there is one player that nobody is talking about who could just be Spurs' next Harry Kane.

Replacing someone of Kane's stature is no mean feat, given he has just won the Ballon d'Or with Bayern Munich to become one of the oldest Ballon d'Or winners. Richarlison, Solanke and now Marmoush have tried to live up to those lofty expectations and it would be unfair to even expect them to get anywhere close to Kane's standards. He is the club's all-time top scorer, after all.

The 26-year-old is 6ft 1ins, one inch shorter than Kane, and has something of a similar path in football to the England captain. Sinayoko has paid his dues in the lower leagues in France, as Kane did in loan spells with the likes of Norwich City, Leyton Orient, Millwall and Leicester City, before making his mark in Ligue Un.

Kane became a revelation in the Premier League at the age of 21, scoring 21 goals in 34 games for Spurs in 2014/15 - Mauricio Pochettino's first season in charge - on his way to becoming one of the greatest Premier League players of all time. Sinayoko started to make his mark aged 23 in 2023/24, scoring nine and assisting five in 35 appearances for Ligue 2 side Auxerre.

The same number of goal contributions followed in 24/25, albeit with five goals and nine assists this time. But that was after a step up to Ligue Un following Auxerre's promotion.

Last season Sinayoko bagged 12 goals and four assists in 32 games, but, aged 26 now, he has shown he is well and truly up to speed in one of Europe's big five leagues. He already has nine goals and five assists in 10 appearances for Paris FC, having made the move in the summer transfer window.

He is the joint third top scorer in Europe's top five leagues this season with nine in the league, the same number as Manchester City star Erling Haaland.

Sinayoko's all-round ability, to score goals and create them, makes him comparable, to a much lesser extent of course, to Kane, while his career trajectory from lower league to the very top, perhaps slightly slower than those who make the grade as teenagers, is also similar. He can also play as a support striker or off the two wings.

Sinayoko is not a name on many people's lips at the moment, but if he carries on his top form, his star will rise. He is unproven in one of the bigger domestic leagues, and that would be a risk for Spurs, but he clearly knows where the goal is and that is what Roberto De Zerbi and Spurs are primarily missing right now.

#1326. Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi said. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ

The new signings at Spurs endured a difficult first few weeks but there were more signs here that they are adjusting to De Zerbi’s system. Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi said. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”

Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

“Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we showed we are a mature team. Maybe we could score more goals with more nastiness, but I am very happy because we created many chances. We need more goals for sure. It’s not enough, but we are improving a lot.

“I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”

When asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender said: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

“The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best plan when you’re down a man.

“Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

“Hopefully, the next game we win. The main message is to stay together as a team. We know what we are capable of. It is staying confident and bouncing back.”

"We want to be back at the top again" Jan Paul van Hecke reacts after Spurs win three consecutive Premier League games ⚪ https://t.co/XXOeOKLhoC

Tottenham have won three Premier League games in a row for the first time in 616 days 📆 https://t.co/krb7tkrPyM

Job done for Spurs, who now have three successive Premier League wins thanks to this routine victory over 10-man Palace. Headers from defensive duo Gray and Van Hecke settled the contest. It was a tricky evening for the visitors and they were left with a mountain to climb following Mateta’s early red card. Tottenham are up to eighth, while Palace are in the relegation zone on goal difference.

FULL-TIME: Spurs make it three Premier League wins in a row! ✅ https://t.co/b44TNkBhqT

Kulusevski cuts inside and whips a shot towards the far top corner, but Henderson is there to make a sensational save and parry it away. Every Tottenham fan wanted that to nestle in the net.

There will be three minutes of added time to end this game.

There’s a double change for Spurs as Udogie and Kulusevski replace Robertson and Kudus.

That should be that. It had been coming ever since the half-time break, and Van Hecke himself might have scored earlier in this game. Bizarrely, he actually scored with his head while sitting on the ground. The Spurs fans enjoyed seeing the replay of that one.

If that does happen, it will open up a lot of space for Spurs in attacking areas. It makes for a very intriguing finale.

Pedro Porro continues to venture forward and smacks a half-volley over from a tight angle. Spurs make the game’s next change as former Palace loanee Gallagher replaces Solanke, with Marmoush moving up into the striker position.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, had some good news for the supporters on Friday when he said that James Maddison was fit and available despite being taken off at Stamford Bridge. “This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.”

While Tottenham are chasing a third successive league victory for the first time in 616 day, De Zerbi insisted there will be no complacency. “For me nothing has changed. We started this pre-season with a long project and we have to stay calm and clear in the head to work to build something better than when we came here,” he said. “One win or one defeat more, nothing will change. We have to analyse to improve the results but to improve the results we have to improve all aspects.”

Pierre Sage, the Palace manager, lightened the load after knocking Fulham out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but seemed surprised that the fans have remained so supportive. “It’s always a good sign,” he said. “I appreciate it [singing his name at Craven Cottage] very much and I can thank them but I prefer they are with the team than me alone. Because I’m the manager, but I’m not the most important part of the team, of the performance and the result. I think the players need it more than me but it’s really appreciated from me.”

Asked what he has learnt about fan sentiment from looking at social media, he said: “I think they understood what happened, why we are not perfect at the moment. We don’t care who is the most responsible for the situation. I take the responsibility. I have no problem with that. I just want people to understand what we do and why.”

Two changes from the starting line-up that took on Newcastle: captain Dean Henderson is back in goal and Oscar Mingueza replaces Anan Khalaili at right wing-back.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.
