#1325. 4 Things Mauricio Pochettino Got Badly Wrong in Liverpool vs Man Utd

An all-smiles Mauricio Pochettino took his seat in the dugout at Anfield, and just eight minutes after kick-off, he wore a face of despair and realised this Manchester United team have a mountain to climb.

Any hope of a new manager bounce coming into effect for United was quickly extinguished by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending off, followed almost immediately by Dominik Szoboszlai's 10th-minute free-kick. Down to ten men, his side conceded a second three minutes later when Florian Wirtz found the back of Senne Lammens' net.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled more misery on the Red Devils, whose new coach has been thrown back into Premier League management in the midst of a crisis. He made some bold decisions heading into today's game against Liverpool, and they played their part in a fifth league defeat of the campaign.

As soon as United released Pochettino's first lineup since his appointment, eyebrows were raised, and Sky Sports' Gary Neville admitted that he'd already conceded defeat upon seeing Matthijs de Ligt chosen in defence. That's not because of the Dutch defender's ability, but rather his lack of football over the past 10 months, having struggled on his return in a 4-1 defeat to Como at the end of October.

De Ligt seems to be shaking off the rust, and starting him at Anfield didn't pan out as Pochettino envisioned. He was largely at fault for Yoro's dismissal, caught way too high up the pitch, allowing Alexander Isak to pounce, burst forward, and buy the foul from De Ligt's defensive partner.

The 27-year-old has endured an injury-ridden spell since joining the club from Bayern Munich in August 2024. A sluggish outing against Liverpool raises question marks over Pochettino's understanding of his squad, especially when picking him over Harry Maguire.

Another head-scratching decision Pochettino made was to start Patrick Dorgu on the left wing. Bryan Mbeumo started over on the right and Matheus Cunha played through the middle, albeit for just 22 minutes before Maguire came on for Mbeumo.

Like De Ligt, Dorgu has similarly been working his way back to full fitness recently after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The Dane is a versatile option, spending the majority of Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back tenure as a left wing-back.

That's not to say Dorgu hasn't impressed occasionally over the course of his United career, and he was probably one of the few positives today. Still, prioritising him over Mbeumo, who scored in this fixture last season, and Cunha, whom Pochettino brought off for Joshua Zirkzee, was rather puzzling.

As was the omission of Shea Lacey, who has been catching the eye every time he's been afforded an opportunity. The English wonderkid can surely do no more, yet even with Amad struggling and benched, he seemingly finds himself third in the pecking order.

This brings us onto Pochettino's substitutions, which caused a stir online, especially the decision to hook Cunha for Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian has been a saviour in the past, most recently coming to the rescue in a 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma.

Cunha showed unbelievable passion that night, even refusing to leave the pitch after receiving a second yellow card for taking his shirt off while celebrating his winner. Of the attackers available to Pochettino right now, he's the one who can make something happen out of nothing.

Mbeumo fell victim to Yoro's sending off, with his new coach forced to bring Maguire on to address the one-man disadvantage. It's difficult to assess whether he'd have had much influence once Liverpool went two-nil ahead, but he's another forward who can come alive when the going gets tough.

Pochettino needs more time with his squad, and decisions such as starting De Ligt over Maguire are clear evidence of this. It's worth pointing out that the Argentine arrived at Carrington on Wednesday, four days prior to the trip to Anfield, and took his first training session on Thursday.

Before that, he took charge of two final games as the United States national team manager, overseeing wins over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals. This isn't so much Pochettino's fault, but for a club sitting 19th and in such a turbulent situation, having him introduced to his squad just four days before a clash with Liverpool is alarming.

United confirmed they came to an agreement with the USMNT for Pochettino to see out his role during the international break, during which only 13 of their 33-man squad were called up. Their official confirmation of his appointment came on November 13th, nine days ago, with the club already languishing in 19th place.

The midfielder made two big claims after his side's defeat at Anfield.

Had they turned to an available coach such as Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte, they surely would have been in the building as soon as the contract was signed. It's a damning example of everything wrong at the club that co-owners INEOS didn't feel it necessary to get Pochettino into Manchester as soon as possible to at least start planning before such a crucial game.

#1323. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

#1322. Rooney, Henry, or Drogba? Nemanja Vidic Named His Toughest Opponent

Former Manchester United defender Nemanja Vidic is considered one of the finest centre-backs in Premier League history, having established himself as a commanding presence through his leadership, physicality and uncompromising defensive style during eight seasons at Old Trafford.

A two-time Premier League Player of the Season, Vidic played a pivotal role in United's success under Sir Alex Ferguson throughout the late 2000s and early 2010s. He helped the Red Devils secure five league championships, the 2008 Champions League trophy and numerous other domestic and European accolades.

Having previously identified Peter Crouch and Luis Suarez among the four toughest opponents of his Premier League career, Vidic was recently presented with another challenge: choosing the most difficult competitor between Thierry Henry, Didier Drogba and Wayne Rooney, three of the greatest strikers in football history.

During a recent conversation with former Manchester United colleague Rio Ferdinand, Vidic was asked to select the toughest opponent from Henry, Drogba and Rooney. He opted for Rooney, explaining that the former England captain's combination of power and pace made him particularly challenging during training sessions:

“Wayne Rooney. Obviously, Didier Drogba, so many big challenges against him, obviously the time we competed, but training every day with Wayne, [he was] powerful, fast.”

Rooney spent the entirety of Vidic's eight seasons at Old Trafford, having arrived from Everton in 2004 for £30.7m, which represented a world-record transfer fee for a teenager at the time.

Both players enjoyed tremendous success in Manchester, collecting numerous team and individual awards. Rooney was named Premier League Player of the Season for 2009/10, while Vidic received the accolade in 2008/09 and 2010/11.

Interestingly, the Manchester United pair only came up against one another away from club football on a single occasion. That meeting came during England's 2-1 friendly victory against Serbia and Montenegro in 2003, when Vidic completed the full 90 minutes and Rooney entered as a second-half substitute for Michael Owen.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Vidic represented Manchester United 300 times, registering 21 goals and collecting 15 major trophies during his spell at the club.

Rooney is widely recognised as one of the most accomplished forwards in Premier League history, having played a defining role in Manchester United's success under Ferguson across his 13 years with the club.

He made an unforgettable start to life at Old Trafford after moving from Everton as a teenager in 2004, finding the net three times on his Champions League debut against Fenerbahce. That performance offered an early glimpse of the remarkable career that followed.

During his time at United, the former England captain collected five Premier League titles, the Champions League in 2008 and the FA Cup in 2016, alongside several other domestic and international honours, including the FIFA Club World Cup in 2008.

Rooney named a United XI brimming with world-class talent and an interesting choice up front.

He also cemented his place in the club's history by becoming Manchester United's all-time leading goalscorer, finishing with 253 goals across 559 appearances and moving beyond Sir Bobby Charlton's previous record of 245 goals in 746 matches.

At international level, Rooney, one of the best English footballers of all time, earned 120 appearances for England and scored 53 goals. He held the national team's goalscoring record until Harry Kane moved ahead of him in 2023.

Rooney brought his professional playing career to an end in 2017 following spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County before transitioning into management. His latest managerial appointment came at Plymouth Argyle in 2024.

#1321. Quantum physics can prove where you are

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Davide Bacco is in the Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Florence, Florence 50019, Italy.

Where you are can matter as much as who you are. Banks, power grids and satellite-navigation systems all depend on knowing where a request or a signal comes from, yet claims about location are notoriously easy to fake. Spoofing and jamming attacks on satellite navigation, for example, are on the rise. Writing in Nature, Kavuri et al.1 report an experiment in which the position of a distant party is certified using the peculiar correlations between quantum particles, known as entanglement. Remarkably, the scheme’s security does not rely on trust of any quantum hardware, only on measurement statistics and the fact that nothing travels faster than light.

#1320. Forget Yoro And De Ligt: Pochettino Must Instantly Axe Dalot at Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Manchester United ended in a disappointing 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Looking to get off to the best possible start, Pochettino's United tenure couldn't have begun much worse. Indeed, the Reds were reduced to ten men in the eighth minute after Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

A long ball over the top of the United back-line caused havoc, and after Matthias de Ligt misread the flight of the ball, Alexander Isak ran through on goal, only for Yoro to bring him down outside the box. As Isak was about to shoot and have a chance at scoring, Yoro hauled him to the floor, and referee Sam Barrott had no choice but to brandish the red card.

From the resulting free-kick, Liverpool went 1-0 up. Dominik Szoboszlai fired the ball through the crowd and into the bottom corner, giving Senne Lammens no chance and sending the Anfield crowd into delirium.

Three minutes later, Liverpool doubled their lead. Rio Ngumoha dribbled past Diogo Dalot with ease before squaring the ball across the face for Florian Wirtz to volley home from close-range.

Liverpool created a number of big chances to extend their lead further, but had to wait until the 66th minute to make it 3-0. Blistering pace from Bradley Barcola saw him steam clear of Lisandro Martinez before squaring for Ngumoha to tap home.

It proved to be another frustrating and difficult evening at the office for Dalot, who let Pochettino down with a dismal performance against Liverpool. Ngumoha - and then Victor Munoz - had so much joy against the Portuguese on Liverpool's left.

Dalot should have done so much better with his defending in the lead-up to Liverpool's second goal. He allowed Ngumoha to have too much space to glide past him on the outside and therefore couldn't get back to block the cross, which led to Wirtz scoring.

Throughout, Dalot couldn't handle Ngumoha. He wasn't able to deal with his pace and threat both on the inside and outside, and even when United defended in a compact shape, he was caught out of position time and time again.

When United pushed to pull one back in the second half, Dalot got caught high up the pitch leading to Liverpool's third goal. His man, Ngumoha, was free in aces of space at the far post and had the simplest of tasks to slot home.

Even after Ngumoha was taken off in the 78th minute, Dalot's evening didn't get much easier. Munoz moved out to the left and was effective against the out-of-form United defender, playing a one-two with Wirtz inside the channel before scoring.

Overall, Dalot was given a dire 5.3 rating by Flashscore, the lowest out of any United player on the pitch. He won just TWO out of his 11 duels, won just two tackles, committed two fouls and was dribbled past twice.

Yoro and De Ligt weren't good, but Dalot was even worse, and he should be taken out of the firing line by Pochettino going into Wednesday's Champions League trip to Sporting CP. Noussair Mazraoui should instead start at right-back.

#1319. Cardinale: ‘I still expect Milan to compete for the Scudetto’

Gerry Cardinale says he still expects Milan to compete for the Scudetto. He also warned that the Rossoneri will only make a January signing if it’s one that genuinely makes a difference.

With quotes via MilanNews, the Milan owner spoke to Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after Sunday evening’s 5-1 win over Frosinone at San Siro. Adrien Rabiot set up two goals as five different players got on the scoresheet. The result lifted Ruben Amorim’s side to fourth on 27 points, three behind Roma and five off leaders Lazio.

“Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight,” Cardinale said.

“I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is really coming together. It’s one game, so we keep the enthusiasm in check, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team, and it’s a team that wants to win right to the end.”

“Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go, but we want to see improvements in every game. This weekend has been very interesting if you look at the results. You can see something is changing in Serie A.

“I was very happy to see us not only win, but win by that margin. We have to build on it. As Amorim says, every game is something to build on.

“Personally, I still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One game at a time. Now the focus is on the Europa League, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are important, and everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to go all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”

Milan now travel to Olympiacos on Thursday, with kick-off at 18:45 CET [17:45 GMT]. Amorim’s side have lost their last two league-phase games, against Bournemouth and Ferencváros, so there is little margin for error in Athens.

Cardinale was also asked whether a new player could arrive in January.

“Again, January is just another stage. As you know, the January market is complicated, so you have to be disciplined. You can’t just throw yourself at something at random.

“The one thing that will happen under my ownership is that whenever we enter the transfer market, we will play to win. That’s the theme I set out at the start of this year. So if we make a move in any window, January or June, it will be a move that counts.”

#1318. Ex-Premier League Referee Issues Verdict On Morgan Rogers Handball

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber believes Michael Oliver made the right decision to award Leeds United a second-half penalty during their thumping 4-1 win at Chelsea.

With the score level after Noah Okafor cancelled out Emmanuel Emegha's opener, Leeds wanted a spot-kick in the 51st minute. It came after Jayden Bogle's powerful shot hit Morgan Rogers, and Leeds felt it struck his arm, while the Chelsea man was insistent it instead came off his shoulder.

But Oliver had no hesitation in pointing straight to the spot, much to the frustration of Rogers and his Chelsea teammates. Video Assistant Referee (VAR) took a closer look at the incident, but agreed with Oliver's initial call and chose not to send him to the screen, believing it was the right decision.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin ended up scoring from 12 yards to put Leeds 2-1 in front. Okafor then added his second to double their advantage, before Brenden Aaronson put gloss on the scoreline late on.

Delivering his verdict on Rogers' handball, ex-Premier League referee Barber said that while he is unsure why VAR didn't advise him to take another look, it wasn't a clear and obvious error, so Oliver made the correct decision.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, Barber said: "You know that I am a real advocate of referees making the big decisions on the field of play and not relying on that. So I applaud Michael [Oliver] for doing that.

"It was at pace and there was a consideration: did he make his body bigger, did it hit the right part of the arm?

"I don’t think it was an obvious error. I think Michael would have quite liked to have seen it, but then the problem is, if you say I think Michael would like to have seen it, then you’ve got VAR coming in and making a decision that isn’t an obvious error.

"We actually want VAR just to come in when it’s really, really obvious. And I think we’re seeing less and less and less of VAR becoming involved because referees are making the decisions on the field of play.

"Most of the time they’re right, and they’re certainly not wrong enough for VAR to come in and interpret and change the on-field decision.

"So for me, I know you like this whole soft penalty and I understand why people say soft penalty, but there isn’t a soft penalty, it’s either a penalty or it isn’t. And for me, I think this was a good decision by Michael, penalty."

#1317. Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

The 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

#1315. A grant to hand out more grants — and build a research area

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Virginia Gewin is a freelance reporter in Portland, Oregon.

Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty

Amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation. The latest development comes from the Experiment Foundation, a non-profit science funding organization in Berkeley, California, which has launched the Field Building Accelerator to cultivate ingenuity hubs around specific fields of research using small, rapidly deployed grants.

The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each. The recipients, in turn, will design their own microgrant programme to distribute up to $10,000 to researchers exploring distinct facets of the same niche scientific problem. The grants will be hosted on Experiment.com, an online platform that allows organizations to advertise and fund research projects.

“We want to create a different persona in science — the people who can chart new research territory,” says David Lang, executive director of the Experiment Foundation.

The accelerator programme is open to proposals that broadly target oceans, climate, toxicity, future science and conservation technology, says Lang — reflecting the interests of its funders, including non-profit organizations such as the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation in Palo Alto, California. Prospective field builders must propose a name for the field, define its core questions and challenges, and identify at least eight researchers, laboratories or communities they would consider funding.

Judges will select field builders who they think are best placed to identify overlooked talent, back unproven ideas and bring like-minded researchers together. Ideally, says Lang, they will reflect diverse scientific perspectives, including early-career researchers, science journalists, science-fiction authors and venture capitalists. “There are people that build momentum in scientific fields, but they are different from the ones who are getting big publications or spinning out companies,” he says.

And, in a bid to take chances on unconventional ideas, the judges will not average scores; instead, if any of the two or three judges champions an application, it moves forward.

Although some might baulk at the idea that $10,000 grants are large enough to spur new research disciplines, others say it is time to experiment with new ways to distribute research funding. “If we really want to help to seed challenging, high risk, ‘who knows what will happen’ ideas, then small-scale grants are a good strategy,” says Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, a non-profit organization in Charlottesville, Virginia, that promotes transparent and reproducible science.

In 2025, The Science Foundation in Seattle, Washington, organized public donations to award up to $10,000 to researchers who have a compelling ‘what if’ basic-science proposal in the areas of mathematics, physical sciences and biological sciences. The foundation announced the second round of winners on 12 November.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

McGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

Torres has already wasted one good chance with his head from eight yards out and there is another. That probably should have found the corner of the net.

Late double change for Fulham as Muniz and Larsson enter the fray.

Aston Villa are also making a late alteration as Garnacho replaces McGinn.

Chance for Aston Villa. Cash clips in a delivery from the right and Torres has a good chance from eight yards out but the Spaniard’s header goes wide.

This game is there for the taking for both sides, although Fulham have been much the better side since the break and currently look more likely to get the winner.

Changes for both sides. For Aston Villa, they bring Barkley on for Kamara.

Fulham meanwhile bring on Palacios and Tete.

Cairney has not been on the pitch long but he is already into the book for cynically bringing down Mbaye.

Cash fouls King and is punished with a yellow card. That is already Cash’s fifth yellow card of the campaign, which means he will miss their trip to Manchester United next weekend.

Fulham are carving Aston Villa open. Bobb drives down their right wing before cutting inside. As he approaches the Aston Villa penalty area, he plays it out to his left to pick out Iwobi in space. Iwobi could hit it first time but instead cuts back onto his right, which allows Cash to block the shot but it does spin behind for a corner.

Before that is taken, Cairney replaces Iwobi. The corner comes to nothing.

Fulham have not made any substitutions yet but based on the way they are playing, they really do not need to right now, unless anyone is exhausted.

You can hear the groans inside Villa Park as the home fans grow frustrated with their side’s performance since the break.

Fulham deserved that equaliser and have been the better side in this game, especially since the break. It does feel like this game is for the taking for Alvaro Arbeloa’s men heading into the final 20 minutes.

Unai Emery has unsurprisingly made a triple change as Mbaye, Buendia and Gomes come on.

The Aston Villa goalkeeper has been outstanding tonight but that is a huge error. The corner is swung in by Iwobi from the left and Suzuki should simply catch it. He backpedals towards his own line and ends up dropping it. By the time he re-gathers, the ball has crossed the line and Fulham have an equaliser that they deserve.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Another save from Suzuki and Fulham spurn yet more great chances. Bobb’s cross from the right side of the box falls right on the head of Iwobi, who should score, but his header is straight at Suzuki. Garcia then has a shot blocked that goes behind for a corner.

An important save from Leno. Maatsen’s volley from the edge of the box takes a deflection off his teammate Torres, forcing Leno into a good reflex save. Had that gone in, it may have been curtains for Fulham.

The chances are piling up for Fulham but they still have not been able to take advantage of any of them. First Bobb has a shot inside the box blocked before Charles curls off target from the edge of the box.

Fulham are really knocking on the door. Bobb and Castagne work it well down the right, with the latter crossing from the right side of the box, forcing Torres to put it behind for a corner. Bobb’s deliveyr beyond the back post is headed back across goal but Aston Villa frantically clear their lines. Aston Villa are under the pump.

You wonder if Unai Emery might turn to his bench imminently as Fulham are on top at the moment.

Fulham once more come agonisingly close to an equaliser. Castange flicks on with his head at the near post from a corner out on the left. Charles then flicks it towards goal but it hits his teammate Garcia and loops over the bar. Alvaro Arbeloa will be wondering how his side are behind in this game.

Fulham have started this half positively and have a corner out on the left. They take it short before Iwobi clips it in but the delivery is poor and easily cleared by Goretzka.

How have Fulham not scored there and got back on level terms? Robinson and Iwobi exchange a neat one-two on the left side of the box before the former sends in a dangerous cross. Suzuki does brilliantly to stick out a hand and the ball flies into the sliding Garcia, ricocheting off the forward and going wide. Suzuki has been crucial for Aston Villa tonight; without him having a good game thus far, Fulham may have scored a couple of times.

Possession: Aston Villa 47%-53% FulhamShots: 7-5Shots on target: 2-1Corners: 5-2Touches in opposition box: 15-14

It’s half time at Villa Park and Unai Emery’s side are 1-0 ahead thanks to that man Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season. But Villa needed Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to be on top form yet again.

Fulham almost took the lead when Antonee Robinson broke clear and crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games.

But Suzuki pulled off another stunning fingertip save following his impressive display against Manchester City last week. Cue a chorus of ‘Zion Suzuki, the world’s No1’ from the Holte End. Wait, wasn’t that Emi Martinez’s song last season?

Villa went ahead five minutes before the break when Jackson powered his way past past two defenders to score after a superb pass from Johan Manzambi released the Senegal striker. Jackson’s fancy footwork created an opening for him to score.

Bassey is into the book late on in the half for a foul on Kamara.

The first half is then brought to an end moments later and Aston Villa lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Jackson’s goal. McGinn did miss a penalty for the hosts whilst Fulham have failed to take a few good chances.

Fulham have had some chances in the first half but have not been able to take advantage of any of them. King has the ball on the right side of the box and tries to pick out Garcia at the far post but there is just slightly too much on the cross.

King has a chance to equalise for Fulham but Suzuki is quick off his line to snuff out the danger. That is two big moments from Suzuki to prevent Fulham from scoring.

There will be four added minutes at the end of this first half.

He scored two against Manchester City a week ago and he now has one tonight. He is found in space on the left by Manzambi and drives into the Fulham penalty area. Both Affengruber and Castagne should probably deal with the danger but somehow allow Jackson to cut inside onto his right and fire into the far corner to put the home side in front.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt

Garcia shoots from the left edge of the box and tries to catch Suzuki out at his near post. Garcia though drags his effort into the side netting as he goes in search of his second Premier League goal.

The Premier League has just posted this on X about the Aston Villa penalty:

VAR: “That’s the hand right up and it hits it”.  AVAR: “For me, his hand is in an unnatural position above his head”.  REF: “After review, Fulham No.16 commits a handball offence with a hand high above the head. The final decision will be penalty kick”.

Fulham should take the lead. Robinson does brilliantly on the counter-attack to drive down Fulham’s left. His ball across the face of the penalty area comes all the way to Bobb, whose first touch is loose but still gets to the ball first. Bobb should score but is denied by Suzuki’s big hand. It is a great save from Suzuku but Bobb should bury that opportunity.

Affengruber brings down Jackson just outside the Fulham penalty area out on the left and the Austrian defender is booked. He tried to plead his innocence but I am not sure he has a leg to stand on with that one.

Aston Villa take it short before McGinn clips in a cross which is headed away.

Fulham wasted a fifth minute chance and may regret it. Gonzalo Garcia crossed for Alex Iwobi who sent his shot over the bar.

Villa awarded a penalty in the 14th after a VAR review when Leon Goretzka’s header hit Sande Berge’s raised hand. No-one appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

But Villa captain John McGinn’s shot hit the crossbar and bounced out again. It was a mystery as to why he took it with Nicolas Jackson available, but Villa are the team on top here.

Fulham are currently having to do a lot of defending, especially negotiating set-pieces. Affengruber is on hand this time to head away McGinn’s corner from the right.

McGinn steps up but his effort smashes into the bar. Leno dived the wrong way but there is too much power and loft on that effort. A massive missed opportunity for Aston Villa and the most relieved man inside Villa Park right now will be Berge.

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY

Berge is pretty close to Goretzka but there is no reason why his arm is above his head like that.

It is adjudged to have been a handball from Berge and Aston Villa are awarded the penalty. That feels like the only decision the referee could come to in all honesty.

Another McGinn corner from the right is met by Goretzka. This time, the German gets his header on target but it is easily saved by his compatriot Leno.

There is a VAR check for a possible penalty. Is there a handball from Berge in there immediately after Goretzka got his head on the ball? It appears that it did strike Berge’s hand and the referee is sent to the screen. We know how this normally goes...

Alysson goes down inside the Fulham box, wanting a penalty, but he is not going to get that.

Aston Villa do have a corner though, which McGinn delivers. His corner is met by Goretzka, who cannot keep his header down and it goes off target.

That is a big early chance for Fulham which Iwobi wastes. Bobb steals possession deep inside his own half and drives forward into the Aston Villa half. He then finds Garcia to his right, who delivers a cross from the right side of the box. There is a nick off Lindelof and comes to Iwobi near the penalty spot but he blazes his effort into the stands. At the very least, Iwobi should be hitting the target.

Is that an example of the time of the game contributing to a decision? Goretzka is pulled back by Garcia, who avoids a yellow card. Had that not been inside the first few minutes of the game, it would not have been a surprise to have seen a yellow card.

After the Remembrance tribute is impeccably observed by those inside Villa Park, we are under way in the final Premier League game of the day.

With this being Aston Villa’s last home league game before Remembrance Sunday, Villa Park pauses to pay tribute to remember the fallen. Wreaths are laid in the middle of the centre circle before The Last Post is played.

As the pyrotechnics go off, both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at Villa Park. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Aston Villa: Suzuki, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Goretzka, Alysson, Manzambi, McGinn, Jackson.Substitutes: Bizot, Harwood-Bellis, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Garnacho, Mbaye, Joao Gomes, Madjo.

Fulham: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, Bobb, King, Iwobi, Garcia.Substitutes: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Rodrigo Muniz, Cairney, Kevin, Larsson, Angel.

Zion Suzuki had big gloves to fill this summer after the sale of Emiliano Martínez but already appears one of the Premier League signings of the summer.

Aston Villa’s new No 1 epitomises the vibrant energy of Unai Emery’s revamped squad and is a goalkeeper perfectly suited to the modern game.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. It started by accusing Carragher of “unacceptable insults to the club and its fans”, then concluded with the vainglorious declaration that “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

ASTON VILLA XI TO FACE FULHAM: Suzuki, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Goretzka, Alysson, Manzambi, McGinn, Jackson

Subs: Bizot, Harwood-Bellis, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Garnacho, Mbaye, Joao Gomes, Madjo

FULHAM XI TO FACE ASTON VILLA: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, Bobb, King, Iwobi, Garcia

Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Rodrigo Muniz, Cairney, Kevin, Larsson, Angel

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”

Emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard said: “For different reasons, not only rest.”

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, has made one change with Sander Berge replacing Hugo Larsson in midfield.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

#1313. The world of Calcio reacts to GTA VI: Corriere dello Sport, Gattuso, De Zerbi & more

Grand Theft Auto VI (or, GTA VI) has finally arrived after 13 years of waiting, and Italian football has joined in on the hype, from the newspaper front pages to the coaches’ press conferences.

As noted by Il Fatto Quotidiano, the game launched at midnight on 19 November. Football quickly caught on. Milan, Inter, Juventus and Lazio all marked the release on social media, Corriere dello Sport turned its Sunday front page into a GTA tribute, and two of Italy’s best-known coaches were asked whether their players would be up all night with a controller in their hands.

Corriere dello Sport’s Sunday front page was the standout. “GTA ttuso 32” was how the paper opened the day after Gattuso’s win over Lecce, playing on the Lazio coach’s name. The 32 refers to Lazio’s points tally, with the Biancocelesti top on their own, “+2 on Gasp and +4 on Chivu”.

Lazio’s 3-0 win was summed up as “Divertimento Lazio”, and “Meraviglia Noslin” was drawn in the style of the video game everyone has been talking about for days. Tijjani Noslin is the main figure in the illustration, with Davide Frattesi and Gattuso embracing behind him.

Milan posted a carousel that turns their players into characters inspired by the look of Grand Theft Auto, captioned “The characters we want in GTA VI”. One image showed Adrien Rabiot driving through Vice City, and another had Strahinja Pavlović at a petrol station. The Rossoneri followed up with “Growing up takes time. So did GTA VI”, a nod to the 13 years since GTA V.

Inter went for a debate instead. Curtis Jones and Djed Spence discussed the series on the way to training: Jones named San Andreas and GTA V as his favourites, while Spence went for Vice City. Juventus, meanwhile, used the game’s graphic style to present Kenan Yildiz and some of his teammates.

If the social media teams were excited, Gattuso clearly wasn’t. Asked in his pre-match press conference before Lecce whether the game might distract his players, the Lazio coach seemed to have no idea what it was.

“I don’t even know what you’re talking about. Is it a video game? I didn’t know. With that name, I thought it was a car,” he said.

“If they play at night, that’s their business. I’m not going to start checking up on them.

“This job requires self-respect. At breakfast together, I’ll try to work out if anyone has been staying up late.”

Asked about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, who had said he would be playing the game after training, Gattuso added: “That’s part of being a professional and caring about your job. I would never tell an individual player not to play.”

Despite all that, Gattuso still ended up in the world of Vice City in a video published by Lazio.

Roberto De Zerbi was more direct. The Tottenham coach was asked the same question at his pre-match press conference before facing Ipswich Town.

“Listen, I am not a policeman, I am not a father, I am a coach,” he said. “I think in my dressing room are good people, mature people, so the PlayStation or other things, the right time they can close, but otherwise I go in their room and I destroy the GTA and the other things.”
